solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: European remix of ‘Lust For Life‘

blocks.note: surface reading: a club DJ's continental reworking of the Iggy Pop song
setter's reading: the phrase lust for life rendered in a European language, here French

explanation.surface: A dance version of Iggy Pop's song made somewhere on the Continent.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Remix' suggests an anagram, but there is no fodder of the right length; the 'remix' is a translation into French.
explanation.definitionFit: The French expression names an exuberant enjoyment of living, exactly what an appetite or zest for existence is.

clue.text: One takes care rubbish is swept up after New Year

indicators.note: in a down clue, being swept up means the word is read from the bottom upwards

blocks.note: JAN is the abbreviation for January, the start of the year
the Roman numeral for one
rot means nonsense or rubbish

explanation.surface: A caretaker clears up the litter left after New Year celebrations.
explanation.walkthrough: 'One' does double duty: it gives I and also starts the definition. JAN + I + TOR (ROT going up) makes JANITOR, and a janitor sweeping up suits the scene.
explanation.definitionFit: A janitor is a caretaker, a person employed to look after and clean a building.

clue.text: Raid or no raid — that needs sorting out

indicators.note: something that needs sorting out is in a muddle, so these letters must be put into a new order

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A commander dithers over whether to attack, a decision still to be settled.
explanation.walkthrough: The repeated word tempts you to look for a double definition; the first 'Raid' is the definition and the second is fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: An inroad is a hostile incursion or sudden attack into enemy territory, the older sense of a raid.

clue.text: Discounts findings

blocks.note: first meaning: amounts taken off a price or a bill
second meaning: conclusions reached by reasoning, as a detective does

explanation.surface: A report on the results of a study of price cuts.
explanation.definitionFit: The word covers both sums subtracted from a total and conclusions arrived at through logical inference.

clue.text: Parking after five in the morning seeing Lorelei?

blocks.note: the Roman numeral for five
am, ante meridiem, marks a morning time
P is the road-sign abbreviation for parking

explanation.surface: A driver who parks just after five a.m. catches sight of someone called Lorelei.
explanation.walkthrough: 'after' places P behind five in the morning, so the pieces read V, AM, P.
explanation.definitionFit: The Lorelei of Rhine legend is a siren luring sailors to ruin, so she is a seductive temptress.

clue.text: Eve flung out without forgiveness

indicators.note: out here means put out of place, so these letters end up in a different order

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Eve was thrown out of Eden and shown no mercy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'flung out' reads as one phrase about expulsion from Eden; only 'out' is the signal and 'flung' is fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone vengeful seeks revenge and so is unforgiving, refusing to pardon a wrong.

clue.text: Stop using space bar function

blocks.note: an em space is a printer's unit of spacing
taken as written
to go means to work or function, as a machine does

explanation.surface: Instructions to halt by pressing the keyboard's space bar.
explanation.walkthrough: 'space bar' looks like one keyboard key, but the words split apart: an em is a typesetting space.
explanation.definitionFit: An embargo is an official ban, a stop placed on trade or on publishing something.

clue.text: Cut in Italy, knight having broken spear died

indicators.note: the knight has broken into the spear, splitting it apart and sitting inside it

blocks.note: I is the international vehicle code for Italy
to gore is to pierce or spear with a horn or tusk
N is the chess notation for a knight
d is the standard abbreviation for died

explanation.surface: A jousting scene in Italy: the knight's lance shatters and he dies.
explanation.walkthrough: I + G(N)ORE + D. 'Cut' as the past tense of snubbing someone, not wounding them.
explanation.definitionFit: To cut someone is to snub them, deliberately ignoring them as if they were not there.

clue.text: Video log I call ‘Nakedly Political‘

indicators.note: stripped naked, the phrase loses its outer covering, its very first and very last letters

blocks.note: the phrase with its opening and closing letters peeled away

explanation.surface: A vlogger announcing the title of their latest openly partisan video.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Nakedly Political' looks like the video's title; 'Nakedly' is the instruction to strip the phrase before it.
explanation.definitionFit: Ideological means concerned with a system of beliefs and doctrine, especially in politics, so it serves as political.

clue.text: Take away about one billion and one carrying over five?

indicators.note: about means around, so the first word wraps round the letters that follow

blocks.note: minus means take away, as in subtraction
I is the Roman numeral for one and B a standard abbreviation for billion

explanation.surface: An arithmetic exercise: subtract a billion, add one, carry over five.
explanation.walkthrough: MIN(I B)US. 'carrying over' sounds like arithmetic carrying, but it means transporting more than five people.
explanation.definitionFit: A minibus is a small passenger vehicle carrying a group, typically more than a car's five seats allow.

clue.text: Gold-digging in sierra, discover sovereign buried by mischief-maker

indicators.note: in a down clue, being buried by something means sitting underneath it, so that word comes later

blocks.note: Sierra is S in the NATO phonetic alphabet
an elf is a mischievous sprite
to see is to discover or find out
a king is a sovereign ruler

explanation.surface: Prospectors in the mountains turn up a gold sovereign coin hidden by a prankster.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Gold-digging' and 'sovereign' (a gold coin) dress the scene as prospecting; a gold-digger is someone after another's money.
explanation.definitionFit: Gold-digging is pursuing a partner for their wealth, which is acting purely out of self-interest.

clue.text: Access transport

blocks.note: first meaning, a noun: a way in, a door or gate
second meaning, a verb with stress on the second syllable: to delight or fill with wonder

explanation.surface: A phrase from a planning notice about getting vehicles in and out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'transport' wants to mean buses; here it is to transport someone with joy, and the answer is pronounced en-TRANCE.
explanation.definitionFit: The noun is a way into a place; the verb means to enchant or carry someone away with delight.

clue.text: Monitor energy needed to replace American gas

indicators.note: one letter is needed to take the place of another, swapping it out of the word

blocks.note: to patrol is to keep watch over an area
E is the physics symbol for energy
A is a standard abbreviation for American

explanation.surface: A call to replace US natural gas with home-grown energy.
explanation.walkthrough: PATROL with its A swapped for E. Americans call the fuel gas, the British call it petrol.
explanation.definitionFit: Gas is the American word for gasoline, the motor fuel the British call by its own name.

clue.text: Champion’s brutal boxing rise

indicators.note: boxing means putting in a box, so the first word encloses the next

blocks.note: vicious means savage or brutal
a tor is a rocky hill, a rise in the land

explanation.surface: A boxing champion's brutal fight brings a rapid rise to fame.
explanation.walkthrough: 'boxing' belongs to the sporting picture, but here it means enclosing; a tor is a hill found on Dartmoor in southwest England.
explanation.definitionFit: Champion used as an adjective describes the winner, one who has triumphed and come out on top.

clue.text: Possibly count half a century or ten times that

blocks.note: L is the Roman numeral for fifty
taken as written
ten times fifty is five hundred, D in Roman numerals

explanation.surface: Instructions for estimating a number: fifty, or maybe five hundred.
explanation.walkthrough: 'count' looks like a verb about numbers; it is the noble title, an example of a lord.
explanation.definitionFit: A count is a European nobleman, an example of a peer addressed by the title of lord.

clue.text: One should enter variation on ‘ludicrous‘

indicators.note: a variation on a word is a version of it with its parts rearranged
entering means going inside, so this letter is placed within the others

blocks.note: the Roman numeral for one
taken as written

explanation.surface: A grammarian ruling that the word ludicrous needs an extra letter.
explanation.walkthrough: The rearranged letters plus I give the answer, and the whole clue also defines it: a variation on 'ludicrous' is a word meaning the same thing.
explanation.definitionFit: Ridiculous and ludicrous are near synonyms, both meaning absurd enough to invite mockery.

clue.text: Passion of revolutionary no one’s welcoming to Germany

indicators.note: welcoming means taking in a guest, so one piece holds another inside it
a revolution turns something right round, so the built string is read backwards

blocks.note: taken as written
the Roman numeral for one
's can stand for has, and has can also be shortened to 've
taken as written
D is the international vehicle code for Germany

explanation.surface: A revolutionary's fervour, with no one welcoming them into Germany.
explanation.walkthrough: No one's = no one has = NO I 'VE; it takes in TO, then D is added and the whole string is reversed.
explanation.definitionFit: Devotion is ardent love or zeal for a person or cause, the same intense feeling as passion.

clue.text: Snaps of red bananas

blocks.note: ginger describes reddish hair
bananas and nuts both mean crazy

explanation.surface: Photographs of ripening bananas, or of red ones.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Snaps' suggests photos; it is ginger snaps, the crisp biscuits that ginger nuts also are.
explanation.definitionFit: Ginger snaps and ginger nuts are the same hard, spicy biscuit (cookie) under two names.

clue.text: Novel character’s name writer used originally in comic sense

indicators.note: originally points to how the word begins, so only its opening letter is kept
comic suggests clowning about, so these letters are jumbled out of order

blocks.note: N is the abbreviation for name
the first letter of writer
taken as written

explanation.surface: A novelist uses a character's name to create a comic effect.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Novel character' sounds like a figure in a book; it means the quality of being novel.
explanation.definitionFit: Newness is the quality of being new or fresh, which is what a novel nature or character has.

clue.text: I would use this before the French loaf

blocks.note: I'd is the contraction of I would
le is French for the

explanation.surface: Advice on whether to put an article before a French loaf of bread.
explanation.walkthrough: 'loaf' looks like bread after 'French'; it is a verb meaning to laze.
explanation.definitionFit: To loaf is to lounge about doing nothing, which is to idle away time.

clue.text: Worshipped standing up and bowing down

blocks.note: in a down entry, the word reads the same going up as going down

explanation.surface: A worshipper standing, then bowing low before an idol.
explanation.walkthrough: The posture words belong to worship, but they really say the answer reads the same up the grid as down it.
explanation.definitionFit: To be deified is to be made a god, and so to be revered and adored as divine.

clue.text: Planks right off the top crumble perhaps

indicators.note: taken off the top means the letter at the head of the word is removed

blocks.note: rafters are the beams or planks supporting a roof
R is the abbreviation for right

explanation.surface: Roof planks with the right one off the top start to crumble.
explanation.walkthrough: 'crumble' reads as a verb about rotten wood; it is the fruit pudding. Afters is British slang for dessert.
explanation.definitionFit: A crumble is a baked fruit dessert, an example of a pudding, which British speakers casually call afters.

clue.text: Rogue male following female

indicators.note: following means coming after, so this piece is placed second

blocks.note: a cow is a female of cattle and similar animals
a boy is a young male

explanation.surface: A rogue bull or stag trailing after a female of the herd.
explanation.walkthrough: In British usage a cowboy is a dodgy tradesman, such as a builder who does shoddy work.
explanation.definitionFit: A cowboy in British slang is an unscrupulous or incompetent worker, a rogue out to cheat customers.

clue.text: In joining RAF, fit inductees get marks written up

indicators.note: in tells you the answer sits inside the run of words that follows

blocks.note: spanning the end of the first word through the start of the last

explanation.surface: Fit new recruits joining the air force are given grades on their reports.
explanation.walkthrough: The RAF is Britain's Royal Air Force. 'marks' looks like scores for recruits; it is scrawls on walls.
explanation.definitionFit: Graffiti are words or drawings scrawled on public walls, marks written up where people will see them.

clue.text: Net fix for boozer?

indicators.note: a drunk slurs speech, so this is the word as a boozer would pronounce it

blocks.note: a fix is a mess, a predicament; slurring the final s turns it into sh

explanation.surface: Asking whether a hangover remedy exists, or for a pub's broken net.
explanation.walkthrough: 'boozer' is British slang for a pub as well as a drinker; here it is the drinker, who slurs.
explanation.definitionFit: Mesh is a material of interlaced threads with open spaces, which is what netting is.

clue.text: Prepare swimmer to go over river, say, moving like the wind

definitions.text: river, say, moving like the wind

indicators.note: going over means flipping across, so the joined words are turned back to front

blocks.note: to edit is to prepare a text for publication
an eel is a swimming fish

explanation.surface: A coach gets a swimmer ready to cross a river, fast as the wind.
explanation.walkthrough: EDIT + EEL read backwards. The definition is a current that runs the same way as the wind blows.
explanation.definitionFit: A lee tide is a tidal stream flowing in the same direction as the wind, a current running with it.

clue.text: Old retired doctor injecting number giving birth

indicators.note: injecting puts something inside, so one piece goes into the middle of another
retired means withdrawn or gone back, so this piece is read backwards

blocks.note: O is the abbreviation for old
a GP is a general practitioner, a family doctor
nine is a number

explanation.surface: An elderly retired doctor gives an injection while a woman is in labour.
explanation.walkthrough: O + G(NINE)P reversed. 'giving birth' is used figuratively: an opening gives rise to something new.
explanation.definitionFit: An opening is a beginning or launch, the act of bringing something into being, as giving birth does.

clue.text: United second — unlikely destiny if that guy’s involved

indicators.note: an unlikely arrangement is an improbable one, so the letters are mixed into an unexpected order

blocks.note: S is the abbreviation for second
taken as written
that guy is he, and he's is the contraction of he is

explanation.surface: A football commentary: Manchester United finish second, an unlikely fate if a certain player features.
explanation.walkthrough: 'United' looks like a football club; it is a past-tense verb meaning combined.
explanation.definitionFit: To synthesise is to combine separate elements into a whole, so synthesised things have been joined together.
